title: REFLEX: Reflexive Equilibrium Fixed-point Learning for Endogenous eXchanges
abstract: arXiv:2608.16155v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In over-the-counter corporate bond markets, dealers compete for client trades by quoting bid and ask prices. Tighter quotes attract more business, but also informed customers more likely to trade ahead of adverse price moves, leaving the dealer holding the risk. As dealers increasingly use machine learning to set quotes, they retrain these models on the trades their own quotes attract, creating a feedback loop in which each model reshapes the market that generates its next training data. The question is therefore not only whether a quoting model performs well, but whether the market it creates stays stable as the model learns from it. Existing performative prediction theory gives a sharp stability condition, yet expresses it through abstract properties of the learning objective a trading desk cannot measure before deployment. translated_title: REFLEX：内生交易中的自反均衡不动点学习
translated_abstract: 在柜台交易的公司债券市场中，交易商通过报价买卖价差来竞争客户交易。更紧的报价会吸引更多业务，但也会吸引更多知情客户，这些客户更可能在不利价格变动前进行交易，从而使交易商承担风险。随着交易商越来越多地使用机器学习来设定报价，他们会根据自己报价所吸引的交易重新训练这些模型，形成一个反馈循环，其中每个模型都会重塑生成其下一个训练数据的市场。因此，问题不仅在于报价模型是否表现良好，还在于当模型从中学习时，它所创造的市场是否保持稳定。现有的表演性预测理论给出了一个尖锐的稳定性条件，但通过交易台在部署前无法测量的学习目标的抽象属性来表达。我们引入了REFLEX，一个框架，用交易市场的三个可测量特征替换那些不可观测的量。
tldr: 本文提出REFLEX框架，通过三个可测量市场特征替代不可观测的稳定性条件，解决内生交易中机器学习报价模型反馈循环的稳定性问题。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces REFLEX, a framework that replaces unobservable stability conditions with three measurable market features to address the stability of machine-learning quoting models in endogenous trading feedback loops.
